title: Playing second trumpet in Angelo Quackalina's reading band
summary: The best reading band he played in used Benny Goodman arrangements, which he learned from records.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you play with many big bands through the years?

The best reading band I ever played with Dick was Angelo Quackalina's Blue Party. They had three brothers, Angelo, Phillip, and Joe. And he, they made friends with the, I think it was an Italian guy who used to arrange for Benny Goodman. And they invited that guy to their house and gave him spaghetti and meatball, pasta basura, whatever you call it. And he gave them all copies of Benny Goodman's arrangements. And boy, those things were written in seven flats, seven shelves, all odd keys. And Angelo says, I know you don't read good, but I happen to have the records that these arrangements came from. So you take the records home and listen to them real good. And I'd have to untwist my fingers sometime after I played the tunes, but I played them so much I memorized them. I was playing second trumpet. But that was the best reading band I ever played in my life. It was a good band when they quit arguing, you know. It was a good band. It wasn't a jazz band.
